fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: When people talk about climate change, they are usually talking about the problem of human-caused global warming, which is happening now. But the climate of the Earth has changed over not just thousands of years, but tens or hundreds of millions of years. It has alternated between hotter and colder periods, with some extremes like ice ages.

Global warming primarily involves the warming of the planet due to increased concentrations of greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere. These gases, like carbon dioxide and methane, come from human activities such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes.

For example, about 60 million years ago there were a lot of volcanoes, which burnt a lot of underground organic matter. Squashed and fossilized dead plants and animals became coal, gas and oil. This caused a lot of carbon dioxide and methane to go up into the air, like nowadays. This made the Earth hot enough for giant tortoises and alligators to live in the Arctic.

Ice ages are long times (much much longer than glaciations) when the Earth got colder, and more ice froze at the North and South Poles. Sometimes even the whole Earth was covered in ice, and was much colder than today.

There is no single reason why there are ice ages. Changes in the Earth's orbit around the Sun, and the Sun getting brighter or dimmer are events which do happen. The angle at which the Earth is tilted compared to the Sun might make a difference. Another source of change is the activities of living things (see Great Oxygenation Event and Huronian glaciation).

Several 19th-century scientists discovered the importance of carbon dioxide (CO2) in climate change. These included Joseph Fourier in 1824, Claude Pouillet in 1827 and 1838, Eunice Foote in 1856, John Tyndall from 1863 onwards, Svante Arrhenius in 1896, and Guy Stewart Calendar (1898–1964).

The Sun gets a little bit hotter and colder every 11 years. This is called the 11-year sunspot cycle. The change is so small that scientists can barely measure how it affects the temperature of the Earth.

If the Sun was causing the Earth to warm up, it would warm both the surface and high up in the air. But the air in the upper stratosphere is actually getting colder. Therefore the changes in the Sun are not causing the global warming which is happening now.

According to the United Nations’ Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the current scientific consensus is that long-term and short-term variations in the Sun's activity play only a very small role in Earth’s climate. Warming from increased levels of human-produced greenhouse gases is actually many times stronger than any effects due to recent variations in solar activity.

For more than 40 years, satellites have observed the Sun's energy output, which has gone up or down by less than 0.1 percent during that period. Since 1750, the warming driven by greenhouse gases coming from people burning fossil fuels is over 270 times greater than the slight extra warming coming from the Sun itself over that same time.

Renewable energy or sustainable energy includes any energy source that cannot be exhausted. This type of energy can remain viable for a long period of time without running out, or lasts forever. Examples are solar, wind, hydropower (water), geothermal, tidal and biomass.

Sunlight from the Sun, when converted, produces solar energy. It is in abundance and freely available. This type of energy is clean and easily renewable. It has low maintenance costs and can generate energy in any climate.
Another clean form of energy is wind. This energy is a plentiful source of renewable energy. However, since it is not always windy, it is only available sometimes.
Through history, the use of wind power has waxed and waned, from the use of windmills in centuries past to high tech wind turbines on wind farms today.

There have been court cases about climate change. At least one case got a verdict at the European Court of Human Rights. The Norwegian government was sued, but won the case in 2025. These kinds of cases are part of Climate change litigation.
resumen_es: Texto divulgativo que distingue entre los cambios naturales del clima de la Tierra y el calentamiento actual causado por el ser humano, descarta que el Sol sea su causa, presenta las energías renovables y menciona los litigios climáticos.
nivel_motivo: Las frases son cortas y sencillas; el nivel léxico lo elevan nombres propios y términos científicos que se entienden por el contexto.

ideas_clave.idea: Although the Earth's climate has always alternated between warm and cold periods, the term usually refers to today's warming, caused by greenhouse gases released by human activities such as burning fossil fuels.
Around 60 million years ago, intense volcanic activity released so much carbon dioxide and methane that the Arctic became warm enough for alligators and giant tortoises.
Ice ages, very long cold periods, have no single cause and may result from changes in the Earth's orbit and tilt, in the Sun's brightness or in the activity of living organisms.
Several nineteenth-century scientists identified the key role of carbon dioxide in the climate.
Variations in solar activity are too small to explain current warming: the upper atmosphere is cooling, and the warming caused by human greenhouse gases is hundreds of times greater.
Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out, such as the sun, wind, water, geothermal heat, tides and biomass.
Solar power is clean and abundant, while wind power is plentiful but intermittent and has been used, in different forms, for centuries.
Climate change has also reached the courts, including a case against the Norwegian government, which it won in 2025.

resumen_modelo: The text explains that, although the Earth's climate has naturally shifted between hot periods and ice ages over millions of years, the expression climate change now usually refers to the current global warming caused by human activity. This warming results from greenhouse gases, mainly carbon dioxide and methane, released by burning fossil fuels, deforestation and industry, a link that scientists had already identified in the nineteenth century. Past changes had various natural causes, such as volcanic eruptions or variations in the Earth's orbit. By contrast, the Sun cannot be blamed for today's warming: its activity varies very little, the upper atmosphere is actually cooling, and human emissions have a far greater effect. As a response, the text presents renewable energies, especially solar and wind power, which are clean and inexhaustible, although wind is not always available. Finally, it notes that climate change has become the subject of court cases.

preguntas.pregunta: Methane is mentioned as one of the greenhouse gases produced by human activities.
preguntas.cita: These gases, like carbon dioxide and methane, come from human activities such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto cita el dióxido de carbono y el metano como gases de efecto invernadero de origen humano.

preguntas.pregunta: What shows how hot the Earth was about 60 million years ago?
opciones: Giant tortoises and alligators could live in the Arctic
The North and South Poles were covered in ice
There were no volcanoes on the planet
The upper stratosphere was getting colder
respuestas: Giant tortoises and alligators could live in the Arctic
preguntas.cita: This made the Earth hot enough for giant tortoises and alligators to live in the Arctic.
preguntas.explicacion: El ejemplo de las tortugas gigantes y caimanes en el Ártico ilustra el calor de esa época. Había muchos volcanes, y el hielo en los polos corresponde a las glaciaciones.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, ice ages are caused by a single factor: changes in the Earth's orbit.
preguntas.cita: There is no single reason why there are ice ages.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto dice que no hay una causa única; la órbita es solo uno de varios factores posibles, junto al brillo del Sol, la inclinación de la Tierra y los seres vivos.

preguntas.pregunta: Which scientist is associated with the year 1856?
preguntas.explicacion: Foote se asocia a 1856. Fourier corresponde a 1824, Arrhenius a 1896 y Tyndall a 1863 en adelante.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 6 una palabra que signifique «apenas, con dificultad».
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning 'only just, hardly'.
preguntas.cita: scientists can barely measure how it affects the temperature of the Earth
preguntas.explicacion: «Barely» significa «apenas»: el efecto del ciclo solar es tan pequeño que casi no se puede medir.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does the cooling of the upper stratosphere suggest that the Sun is not causing current global warming?
respuestas: If the Sun were responsible, both the surface and the upper atmosphere would be getting warmer; since the upper stratosphere is actually cooling, the warming must have another cause.
preguntas.cita: If the Sun was causing the Earth to warm up, it would warm both the surface and high up in the air.
preguntas.explicacion: Es un razonamiento por contraste: el patrón observado (superficie más cálida, estratosfera más fría) no coincide con el que produciría el Sol.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: According to the IPCC, variations in the Sun's activity play a major role in the Earth's climate.
preguntas.cita: variations in the Sun's activity play only a very small role in Earth’s climate
preguntas.explicacion: El IPCC considera que el papel de la actividad solar es muy pequeño, no importante.

preguntas.pregunta: Since 1750, how does greenhouse-gas warming compare with extra warming from the Sun?
preguntas.cita: is over 270 times greater than the slight extra warming coming from the Sun itself over that same time
preguntas.explicacion: El calentamiento por gases de efecto invernadero es más de 270 veces mayor. 40 son los años de observación por satélite y 0,1 % la variación de la energía solar.

preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'being used up completely'.
preguntas.cita: This type of energy can remain viable for a long period of time without running out
preguntas.explicacion: «Run out» significa agotarse o acabarse; aquí aparece en gerundio tras «without».

preguntas.explicacion: El texto dice que la energía solar tiene bajos costes de mantenimiento, pero no compara costes de instalación con la eólica.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the main drawback of wind energy mentioned in the text?
opciones: It is only available when it is windy
respuestas: It is only available when it is windy
preguntas.cita: since it is not always windy, it is only available sometimes
preguntas.explicacion: El inconveniente es la intermitencia. El texto la presenta como limpia y abundante, y los costes de mantenimiento se mencionan a propósito de la solar.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 13 una expresión que signifique «ha crecido y disminuido alternativamente».
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'increased and decreased over time'.
preguntas.cita: the use of wind power has waxed and waned
preguntas.explicacion: «Wax and wane» procede de las fases de la Luna (crecer y menguar) y se usa para cosas que aumentan y disminuyen con el tiempo.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the last paragraph suggest about the role of courts in climate change?
respuestas: It suggests that climate change has become a legal issue, with cases brought against governments and even reaching the European Court of Human Rights; for example, the Norwegian government was sued, although it won in 2025.
preguntas.cita: There have been court cases about climate change. At least one case got a verdict at the European Court of Human Rights.
preguntas.explicacion: La idea es que el cambio climático ya se dirime también en los tribunales («climate change litigation»).
